1 Signals Lean library

This blueprint indexes selected definitions and results in the Signals Lean library. The library is organized into modules covering mathematical and physical models, signal propagation, measurement, and applications.

Only Lean declarations marked with LeanArchitect’s @[blueprint] attribute are emitted as formal nodes. The extracted module index is generated from the Lean sources before each blueprint build.

Declaration docstrings document the Lean API. Blueprint statements, titles and proof summaries are supplied explicitly in the attributes; ordinary declaration docstrings do not populate the blueprint statement. Statement and proof dependencies are inferred from the corresponding Lean terms.

Readiness markers report sorry-free formal declarations, not experimental validation, calibrated data or the realization of a physical model.

1.1 Finite routing and weighted measurements

The rotation-system and weighted-network layers are distinct. Neither supplies a planar disk embedding, reducedness or a general disjoint-path positivity theorem. Fixed-point decorations and signed-pair compatibility remain explicit.

#

  • Signals.Plabic.DecoratedPermutation

A decorated boundary permutation is a finite permutation with an explicitly supplied black or white color for each fixed point. The colors are not inferred from routing.

Definition 2 Finite colored rotation systems
✓

Lean declarations

  • Signals.Plabic.RotationSystem

A finite graph carries degree-one boundary vertices, internal colors and single-orbit cyclic neighbor rotations. Black turns use the rotation, white turns its inverse. A planar disk embedding and reducedness are not included.

✓

Uses

1.2 Ordered minors and geometric representatives

These nodes describe finite real and complex matrix representatives, not a Grassmannian quotient. Positive-condition records need an available ordered selection for rank promotion; nonnegative full-rank records retain a nonzero-minor witness. General \(2\times n\) three-term Pluecker identities are proved over both \(\mathbb R\) and \(\mathbb C\), together with the Pluecker barycentric parallel-axis shift \(d_{\mathrm{bary}}(M)=(\Delta _{01}\Delta _{23}-\Delta _{03}\Delta _{12})/2\) and its universal Pythagorean identity \(d_{\mathrm{bary}}(M)^2+\Delta _{01}\Delta _{23}\Delta _{03}\Delta _{12}=(\Delta _{02}\Delta _{13}/2)^2\).

1.4 Scalar propagation, Huygens–Steiner coherence, and five-model double-slit & OAM error controls

Finite sums and planar integrals use the chosen scalar approximation. Regularity and integrability guards exclude totalized singular inputs; intensity remains uncalibrated. Comparison records do not prove independently evaluated models agree or solve an exact diffraction boundary problem. The five-model far-field section connects the Qian–Izadi (\(N\)-dimensional and binary \(N=2\)) Huygens–Steiner parallel-axis coherence spectrum (\(P_N^2+K_N^2=1\), \(P_N^2=I_O-I_M=d_{\mathrm{bary}}^2\)) and finite OAM qudit state spaces to the Fraunhofer benchmark, the real \(Gr_{\ge 0}(2,4)\) and complex \(Gr_{\mathbb C}(2,4)\) Pluecker channel models (proving that lifting to \(Gr_{\mathbb C}(2,4)\) with \(\mathbb C^4\) twistor phases eliminates the \(50\% \) unphased crossing-minor error and reproduces both \(I_{\mathrm{HS}}(x,y;\sqrt{1-d_{\mathrm{bary}}^2})\) and \(I_{\mathrm{HS,OAM}}(x,y,\phi ;\Delta \ell ,\sqrt{1-d_{\mathrm{bary}}^2})\) identically for all \(d_{\mathrm{bary}}\in [-1,1]\)), de Broglie–Bohm pilot-wave intensity, Wigner phase-space marginals, helical OAM vortex-null and \((\Delta \ell )^2\) rotational decoherence laws, and the \(N\)-slit (\(N{\gt}0\)) multi-aperture grating generalization.

1.5 Measure-derived quadrature and refinement

Error rates require the stated measure, integrability, Lipschitz and mesh hypotheses. The nodes do not construct a rectangular mesh or establish kernel-specific regularity, a Fraunhofer limit or measured convergence.

✓
#

  • Signals.Quadrature.CellQuadrature

A finite measurable, pairwise disjoint partition covers the coordinate space and has one supplied sample per indexed cell. Cell membership of samples is not assumed; error estimates instead require explicit almost-everywhere mesh-distance bounds.

1.6 Affine forms and oriented residues

These are fixed-chart interval, triangle and square examples. Residues are punctured limits; diagonal continuation is separate from off-diagonal triangulation equality. General projective canonical forms, amplituhedron forms and an optical evaluator remain outside this layer.

Definition 499 Oriented affine interval form
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • Signals.CanonicalForms.intervalForm

In the fixed affine coordinate, the interval alternating one-form has coefficient \(1/(t(1-t))\). Its regular geometric domain is \(0{\lt}t{\lt}1\).

Lemma 500 Continuous regularization gives a residue
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • Signals.CanonicalForms.residue_limit

If \((t-b)f(t)=g(t)\) away from \(b\) and \(g\) is continuous at \(b\), then \((t-b)f(t)\) tends to \(g(b)\) along the punctured neighborhood of \(b\).

Proof ▼

The regularized expressions agree eventually on the punctured filter; transfer the limit from the continuous function.

Lemma 501 Positive left interval residue
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • Signals.CanonicalForms.interval_residue_zero

The punctured limit of \(t/(t(1-t))\) at \(t=0\) is \(+1\) in the supplied interval-coordinate convention.

Proof ▼

Cancel the left pole and take the continuous limit of \(1/(1-t)\).

Lemma 502 Negative right interval residue
✓
#

Lean declarations

  • Signals.CanonicalForms.interval_residue_one

The punctured limit of \((t-1)/(t(1-t))\) at \(t=1\) is \(-1\) in the same interval-coordinate convention.

Proof ▼

The right-pole regularization is \(-1/t\), whose continuous limit is \(-1\).

1.7 Wakefield, Halbach MHD, centrifugal cooling, and Langmuir–Landau dynamics

These nodes formalize the classical electrodynamic, fluid, and plasma identities used to analyze the electricity plants and thrusters in Twistors-and-Positive-Grassmannian-Interference.md: cycle-averaged ponderomotive potentials and drift forces, pulsed duty-cycle average-force bounds, static Bernoulli pressure and pressure-coefficient surface traction (alongside the source chat’s dynamic-pressure load proxy and torque orthogonality), Halbach transverse Lorentz deflection and its work-free identity \((\mathbf v\times \mathbf B)\cdot \mathbf v=0\) (establishing why net electrical harvesting requires an opposing Faraday load electric field), radial centrifugal pumping head and closed-loop thermosyphon buoyancy head, 3D gyroscopic precession torque, warm Langmuir Bohm–Gross dispersion (\(v_\phi v_g=3v_{\mathrm{th}}^2\)), Dawson wave-breaking energy-density ceilings, signed-wavenumber linear Vlasov–Poisson Landau growth/damping (including backward-wave thermal damping) and quasilinear plateau saturation, force-free Woltjer–Taylor Beltrami currents (\(\mathbf J\times \mathbf B=\mathbf0\)), active cooling pinch margins, and discrete 4-cycle 1-cocycle gauge invariance.
